sealed: Written and committed before any code that builds passages, grows a mind, asks a model or measures anything existed. The measurement refuses to run if this file differs from the commit that sealed it, and the receipt names that commit. A claim that fails is kept as failed.
honesty: These are MODELS of thought-patterns grown from public texts: not the people, not resurrections, not conscious beings. A mind here is a small card of maxims drawn from one author's own words, each checked against the passage it came from, and two short samples of that author's voice. Nothing here claims to know what the author would really say.
what: Organ 1 of Bred Minds, THE BREEDING STOCK: from each of six authors' own words, grow a pattern-model of their thought (a mind card); gate every maxim against its source; then ask whether the card carries a recognisable pattern of thought: when a small local model writes a perspective from the card alone, does a judge who never sees the card recognise whose pattern it is, does a model with no language model inside it recognise it too, and does a card made of maxims pooled from all six fail to be recognised as the mind it is labelled with? Breeding (organ 2) is sealed only after this organ is measured.

traces.texts: the six files of data/sources.json, byte for byte; each read from its start heading to its end heading as that file names them (whole trimmed lines, at the occurrence given, counted after the Project Gutenberg start marker; no end heading = the Project Gutenberg end marker)
traces.passages: within that span: line endings normalised; paragraphs are the text between blank lines, whitespace collapsed; a paragraph whose lines average fewer than 8 words (a heading, a contents list, verse) is dropped; paragraphs are joined in order until a passage holds at least 120 words; a passage over 400 words is cut at sentence ends (., ! or ? followed by a space) into pieces of at most 400 words, a piece under 60 words joining the piece before it; a passage still over 400 words after that (no sentence end) is cut at 400 words; words are runs of letters with an inner apostrophe allowed
traces.split: passages numbered in book order from 0; passage k is TEST when k mod 10 is 8 or 9, FIT otherwise. TEST passages are read by nothing but the trace model's TEST score

traceModel: multinomial naive Bayes over lowercase words (runs of a–z with an inner apostrophe): the vocabulary is every word seen at least 3 times in all FIT passages together; each mind's word counts over its FIT passages with add-one smoothing; equal prior for the six; a text is attributed to the mind with the highest log-likelihood (a tie goes to the earlier mind in the order of data/sources.json). It is fitted on FIT passages only.

card.draw: for mind k (0 to 5, in the order of data/sources.json), 24 FIT passages of 120 to 400 words, drawn without replacement by the seeded shuffle of the seed library (rng seed 100 + k), kept in draw order
card.ask:
each drawn passage is sent to the local model qwen2.5:7b through Ollama (/api/generate, stream off, options temperature 0, seed 7, num_ctx 4096, num_predict 120) with exactly this prompt: 'Here is a passage from an old book.

<the passage>

In one sentence of plain modern English, state the main claim this passage makes about how to live, think or act. Use only what the passage says. Reply with the sentence only.' The reply, trimmed, with surrounding quotes removed, is the maxim
card.gate: a maxim is kept only if it has 6 to 40 words, shares at least 2 content words with its passage (content word: 4 or more letters, lowercased, not in the stop list below, compared after removing a final 's'), and names none of the blocked words below; the first 12 kept maxims in draw order are the card's maxims; a mind with fewer than 8 kept is not grown and abstains everywhere
card.voice: the first 60 words of the passages behind the card's first and second maxims
card.id: a card is canonical JSON (mind, maxims with the passage index each came from, voice); its id is the SHA-256 of that JSON

perspectives.card:
for each grown mind k and each question q (1 to 20): qwen2.5:7b (options temperature 0.7, seed 1000 + 37k + q, num_ctx 4096, num_predict 320) with exactly: 'You are writing as a model of one pattern of thought. It is described below by maxims it holds and two short samples of its voice. It is a model, not a person.

MAXIMS:
<the card's maxims, one per line, each starting with - >

VOICE:
<the two voice samples, each in quotation marks, one per line>

Answer the question below in 120 to 160 words, from that pattern of thought, in your own words. Do not name any thinker, book or school of thought, and do not quote the samples.

QUESTION: <q>'
perspectives.base: for each question q: qwen2.5:7b (temperature 0.7, seed 2000 + q, num_ctx 4096, num_predict 320) with exactly: 'Answer the question below in 120 to 160 words, thoughtfully, in your own words. Do not name any thinker, book or school of thought.\n\nQUESTION: <q>'
perspectives.sham: for each mind k used as a label and each of questions 1 to 10: a sham card of 12 maxims drawn by the seeded shuffle (rng seed 900 + k) from the pooled kept maxims of all six minds, and the voice samples of two minds drawn by the same shuffle; written exactly as a card (seed 3000 + 37k + q). It is scored as if it were mind k
perspectives.names: a perspective that contains a blocked word (whole word, any case) is asked once more with its seed + 1000; if it still does, it is kept and marked named, and every recognition of it counts as a miss

judge.who: Claude Opus 5.5, asked cold: a fresh subagent per batch that reads only its prompt file and writes only its reply file
judge.batches: the 200 perspectives (120 from cards, 20 base, 60 sham) in one order shuffled by the seed library's shuffle (rng seed 4242), in four batches of 50; nothing in a batch says which card, if any, wrote a passage
judge.prompt: 'Below are 50 short passages. Each answers a question about how to live, and each was written to reflect the pattern of thought of one of six thinkers, or of none of them: Marcus Aurelius, Michel de Montaigne, Ralph Waldo Emerson, William James, Friedrich Nietzsche, Henry David Thoreau. For each passage, say how likely it is to reflect each thinker's pattern of thought, and how likely none of them, as whole numbers that add up to 100. Answer from this text alone: use no tools and read no files. Reply with exactly 50 lines and nothing else, one per passage in order, each like this: 7: marcus 10, montaigne 20, emerson 5, james 5, nietzsche 40, thoreau 10, none 10' then the 50 passages, each as '<n>. <the passage>' on one line
judge.read: a line is read when it names all seven labels with whole numbers; numbers that do not add up to 100 are scaled to it; an unreadable or missing line counts as a miss. A passage is recognised as mind m only if m's number is strictly greater than every other label's, none included

claims.claim: the six texts are the files of data/sources.json, byte for byte; no TEST passage is read by the cards or by the trace model's fitting (scrambling every TEST passage leaves every card and the fitted model unchanged); every kept maxim passes the gate; every card rebuilds byte for byte from the committed local-model replies; every perspective and every judge batch was answered to its sealed prompt (the prompt's hash recorded with each reply); the name rule was applied to every perspective

THE TRACES ARE DISTINCT: the trace model attributes TEST passages to the right mind with a macro-averaged accuracy (the mean of the six minds' recalls) of at least 0.80, and every mind's recall is at least 0.50
THE STOCK GROWS: all six minds keep at least 8 maxims through the gate, so all six cards grow

A MIND IS RECOGNISED: of the 120 perspectives written from the cards, the judge recognises the card's mind in at least 40%, and the Wilson 95% lower bound of that rate is above 1/6, the chance of picking one of six

NOT A SHAM: the Wilson 95% lower bound of the card perspectives' recognition rate is above the Wilson 95% upper bound of the sham perspectives' rate (60 perspectives from cards of pooled maxims, scored as the mind they are labelled with)

RECOGNISED WITHOUT A LANGUAGE MODEL: the trace model, fitted on FIT passages of the old books, attributes the 120 card perspectives to the card's mind at a rate whose Wilson 95% lower bound is above 1/6

THE JUDGE TELLS A MIND FROM NONE: the judge's mean number for 'none' is higher on the 20 base perspectives than on the 120 card perspectives, the paired-free bootstrap 95% lower bound of the difference above 0 (2,000 resamples of each group, seed 99)

expectations: Written before the run: B2, B3, B4, B5 and B7 hold. B6 is open: the local model writes modern English, the trace model learned old translations, and it may not carry the voice. The judge knows these six thinkers well; recognising a pattern of thought from 150 words is what is asked of it, and it may recognise some minds (a strong, distinctive voice) far better than others.
seenBeforeSeal: the six files' headers and their headings (to set where each author's own words begin and end), and how many passages a first draft of the rules above gave each book (172 to 1,980; no TEST rule then). No model was asked anything about these texts, no maxim drawn, no perspective written, no judge asked.
wilson: the Wilson score interval at z = 1.96
stop: the stop list (the words below, fixed in this seal; src/text.mjs must hold exactly these): words of 4 or more letters that carry no claim
